summary: Theory 11, written in the statistician's role, sets the inference standards the whole bridge programme is held to: naming the correct within-stratum estimand, defining an informative stratum, Mantel-Haenszel stratification with a finer stratification variable giving 13x more informative strata, a three-part replication rule replacing sign-only replication, declared and disclosed effect-size floors, an estimator-hygiene register (N_viol exact vs biased Ĥ, invalid bootstrap CI), the confounding standard against overgeneralizing regime-specific findings, and the finding that power is a property of the informative region rather than of sample size.
contribution_assessment: Methodology chapter assembled from what actually caught errors across the KR-BRIDGE programme; formalizes several standards (within-stratum estimand, replication-with-magnitude, confounding scope discipline) as reusable statistical rules for the whole research lane.

summary: Theory 10 assembles the programme's experimental-methodology rules from what actually caught real errors: pre-registration amendments (labels as classifications-to-be-tested, no generator tuning to balance cells), a ten-item control checklist with the perturbation-verified-provenance control singled out as this cycle's most valuable, four rules born of specific past errors (within-stratum adjudication, triple-based admissibility, magnitude-constrained replication, structurally-inapplicable-vs-refuted), a generalized provenance check shown to both dissolve and strengthen findings, the new frozen O-F* experimental protocol (Estimand Non-Degeneracy Preflight) with two stated research-governance safeguards evidenced by KR-ZOOM-03 and KR-ZOOM-OUT-01 near-misses, and the standing EXPERIMENT->AUDIT->ADJUDICATION->THEORY v1.3 governance order.

summary: Part I of the KnowledgeOS v2.0 theory rewrite: establishes the foundational semantic-separation axioms (Reality/Observation/Information/Evidence/Knowledge/Decision/Action; Truth/Evaluation/Determination/Decision), proves that observation need not be injective (Prop 3.1) and that representation loss defeats required distinctions (Thm 16.1), redefines the Knowledge Gap set-theoretically as unsatisfied requirements (rejecting the prior subtraction formulation), defines contract-relative Zero and proves its basic gap-equivalence/reduction theorems with an explicit contract-compatibility caveat, states history-preservation as replacing universal epistemic monotonicity, freezes the five-operation core interface, and formally withdraws the prior unique-minimal-kernel claim about ABK-1 in favor of 'validated candidate-adequate.'
contribution_assessment: Opens the full formal KnowledgeOS v2.0 rewrite; introduces the first proved theorems (3.1, 16.1, 24.1, 25.1) and eight numbered foundational axioms (A1-A8) that all later Parts (II-XVII) build on.

summary: Part II gives Parts I's distinctions a formal many-sorted type system (22 semantic sorts from Entity to Action), proves four theorems (2.1 representation-does-not-imply-arithmetic, 2.2 type safety of typed relations, 2.3 semantically-lossy-representation generalizing Thm 16.1, 2.4 non-monotonic evolution, 2.5 locality of contradiction), defines Epistemic Status as explicitly non-totally-ordered and contract-relative, and closes with ten Foundational Type Invariants (I1-I10) protecting the ontology from collapsing into an ordinary database.
contribution_assessment: Second installment of the v2.0 rewrite; formalizes the sort/type layer underlying every later Part and supplies the representation-adequacy theorem (2.3) that Parts V/VIII repeatedly cite.

summary: Part III formalizes epistemic semantics as five explicit layers (Truth, Evidence, Evaluation, Determination, Decision) rather than one binary logic, defines conditional/assumption-dependent knowledge and justification-as-graph, separates four distinct uncertainty concepts, imposes a strict 'no probability without a probability model / no estimator without an estimand' statistical discipline, forbids inferring independence from distinct records, proves the culminating Epistemic Non-Collapse theorem (3.3, status never implies truth without an explicit soundness bridge), and proposes four candidate DDD bounded contexts plus an anti-corruption-layer example for external status fields.
contribution_assessment: Third installment of the v2.0 rewrite; the Evidence->Evaluation->Determination->Decision pipeline and Theorem 3.3 are reused throughout Parts V-VI and beyond.

summary: Part IV formalizes KnowledgeOS as a labeled transition system 𝒦=<S,Λ,→,S0>: rejects the naive current-facts-only knowledge state in favor of K=<Current,History,...>, gives formal definitions and preconditions for the five core operations (with ASSERT!=ACCEPT, REVISE!=overwrite, RETRACT!=DELETE, ISOLATE!=rejection), proves state-validity preservation (4.1) and history preservation (4.2) theorems, establishes operation non-commutativity and per-operation idempotence, and proves a reproducibility theorem (4.3, replay reconstructs state under determinism plus preserved rule versions).
contribution_assessment: Fourth installment; the transition-system formalism (delta, Pre, Valid, the five operations with formal preconditions) is the operational backbone that Parts V-VII build gap algebra, revision and identity semantics on top of.

summary: Part V rigorously builds the Knowledge Gap as a power-set/lattice algebra over contract-relative requirements: defines contract-relative requirement sets and generalized (non-Boolean) satisfaction, proves gap containment is only a partial order, explicitly corrects the tempting assumption of monotone gap reduction (gap expansion can be epistemically positive), establishes the fixed-universe gap lattice with Zero as its bottom element, defines the 'False Zero' governance failure mode requiring an auditable Zero trace, and proves a Conditional Zero Preservation theorem under four named stability assumptions, closing with twelve constitutional statements (V-C1..V-C12).
contribution_assessment: Fifth installment; the fixed-requirement-universe gap lattice (Zero=bottom element) and the False-Zero/auditability requirement are the part's most load-bearing new formal results, directly used by Part VI's local/global Zero equivalence.

summary: Part VI formalizes the full Evidence->Evaluation->Satisfaction->Determination calculus: evidence relations, quality dimensions, independence, and aggregation (rejecting additive strength by default), Determination Definition 6.2 with its Gap-Equivalence Theorem 6.1 and Requirement-Complete/Sound Determination theorems (6.2, plus a conditional soundness bridge), a six-class epistemic error taxonomy, Determination and Evidence recast as rich domain concepts rather than Boolean flags or generic records, and formal forward/reverse requirement-to-evidence traceability enabling scoped re-evaluation, closing with fourteen constitutional statements (VI-C1..VI-C14).
contribution_assessment: Sixth installment; supplies the formal apparatus (Det, Delta_p, the six error classes, traceability) that Parts VII and beyond reuse for revision, retraction and dependency propagation.

summary: Part VII (read via introduction, a full first-half pass through §7.1-7.11 on revision/retraction, a grep-derived section map of the remaining ~90 subsections covering temporal validity/bitemporal semantics/contradiction/conflict/isolation/belief revision/dependency graphs/DDD implications, and the closing constitutional summary and Part-VIII transition) formalizes revision, retraction, temporal validity and non-monotonic knowledge evolution: historical preservation (H_t⊆H_{t+1}) is proved to coexist with epistemic non-monotonicity, REVISE/RETRACT are formally distinguished from deletion and from falsity, data growth is shown not to imply knowledge monotonicity, and event/knowledge/valid/transaction time are introduced as the Part's temporal vocabulary.
contribution_assessment: Seventh installment of the v2.0 rewrite.
